bank.name: Salah, Zakat, Hajj & Fasting Details
bank.subject: Islamic Studies
bank.description: Detailed questions on the practical pillars of Islam — prayer, alms, pilgrimage and fasting.

questions.prompt: How many obligatory (Fard) prayers are there in a day?
questions.explanation: Muslims pray five obligatory prayers daily: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

questions.prompt: How many Rakat are in the Fajr prayer?
questions.explanation: Fajr consists of 2 Sunnah and 2 Fard rakat.

questions.prompt: How many Rakat are in the Maghrib prayer?
questions.explanation: Maghrib has 3 Fard rakat plus 2 Sunnah, prayed after sunset.

questions.prompt: Which prayer is prayed in the middle of the night and is optional but highly recommended?
questions.explanation: Tahajjud is the voluntary night prayer, praised in the Quran (17:79).

questions.prompt: The two Eid prayers are known as?
questions.explanation: Eid-ul-Fitr follows Ramadan; Eid-ul-Adha follows the Hajj season.

questions.prompt: What is 'Tayammum'?
options: Dry ablution with clean earth when water is unavailable
questions.explanation: Tayammum is the dry ablution performed with clean soil when water is not available.

questions.prompt: What is the direction Muslims face during prayer called?
questions.explanation: The Qibla is the direction of the Kaaba in Makkah, faced during prayer.

questions.prompt: Zakat is how many percent of one's eligible wealth?
questions.explanation: Zakat is 2.5% (1/40) of qualifying wealth held for a lunar year.

questions.prompt: Zakat is compulsory on savings above which threshold?
questions.explanation: Nisab is the minimum wealth threshold above which Zakat becomes obligatory.

questions.prompt: Zakat is the ________ pillar of Islam.
questions.explanation: The five pillars: Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm, Hajj — Zakat is the third.

questions.prompt: Fasting (Sawm) is the ________ pillar of Islam.
questions.explanation: Sawm (fasting in Ramadan) is the fourth pillar of Islam.

questions.prompt: What is 'Suhoor'?
options: The meal to break the fast
questions.explanation: Suhoor is the meal eaten before dawn (Fajr) to prepare for the day's fast.

questions.prompt: What is 'Iftar'?
options: The evening meal that breaks the fast
questions.explanation: Iftar is the meal eaten at sunset to break the day's fast.

questions.prompt: What is 'Taraweeh'?
options: The special night prayer in Ramadan
questions.explanation: Taraweeh is the voluntary night prayer performed during Ramadan.

questions.prompt: Fasting is obligatory for which month?
questions.explanation: Fasting in Ramadan is the fourth pillar, prescribed in Surah Al-Baqarah 2:183.

questions.prompt: Hajj is the ________ pillar of Islam.
questions.explanation: Hajj is the fifth pillar, obligatory once in a lifetime for those who can afford it.

questions.prompt: The white garment worn by pilgrims is called?
questions.explanation: Ihram is the two-piece seamless white garment worn by pilgrims, symbolizing equality.

questions.prompt: Circumambulating the Kaaba seven times is called?
questions.explanation: Tawaf is the seven circuits around the Kaaba; Sa'i is running between Safa and Marwah.

questions.prompt: Running between the hills of Safa and Marwah is called?
questions.explanation: Sa'i commemorates Hajar's search for water for Isma'il (AS).

questions.prompt: Standing at Arafat on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah is called?
questions.explanation: The standing at Arafat is the essence of Hajj — 'Hajj is Arafat'.

questions.prompt: What is 'Umrah'?
questions.explanation: Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage, optional and performable at any time of year.

questions.prompt: Where do pilgrims sacrifice animals on Eid-ul-Adha?
questions.explanation: The sacrifice (Qurbani) on 10-12 Dhul-Hijjah is performed in Mina.

questions.prompt: Stoning the three pillars (Jamarat) at Mina is called?
questions.explanation: Rami al-Jamarat is the ritual stoning of pillars symbolizing the rejection of Satan.

questions.prompt: How many days are the days of Tashreeq?
questions.explanation: The days of Tashreeq are 11, 12 and 13 Dhul-Hijjah, following Eid-ul-Adha.

questions.prompt: What is 'Kaffarah'?
options: A penalty, e.g. for breaking a fast without excuse
questions.explanation: Kaffarah is the expiation/penalty required for certain violations such as breaking a fast deliberately.

questions.prompt: How many times does the Adhan call 'Hayya ala-s-Salah' (come to prayer)?
questions.explanation: 'Hayya ala-s-Salah' is said twice in the standard Adhan.

questions.prompt: What is said after the Adhan as a recommended supplication?
options: The Dua of Wasilah for the Prophet (PBUH)
questions.explanation: After the Adhan, believers ask Allah to grant the Prophet (PBUH) the Wasilah.

questions.prompt: The minimum number of people for congregational Jumu'ah in Hanafi fiqh is?
questions.explanation: Hanafi scholars require at least three men besides the imam for Jumu'ah.

questions.prompt: What is the reward for fasting the month of Ramadan according to hadith?
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said fasting Ramadan with faith expiates past sins.

questions.prompt: What is 'Fidyah' for those unable to fast?
options: Feeding a poor person per missed fast
questions.explanation: Fidyah is feeding one needy person per unkept fast for the permanently unable.

questions.prompt: Which act is done during Hajj at Mina on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah?
questions.explanation: On Eid day, pilgrims stone the Jamarat and offer the sacrifice.

questions.prompt: The 'Talbiah' is the chant recited by pilgrims. What is its opening?
questions.explanation: 'Labbaik Allahumma Labbaik' — Here I am, O Allah, here I am — is the Talbiah.

questions.prompt: The Kaaba is also called?
questions.explanation: The Kaaba is Baitullah, the sacred House of Allah in Makkah.

questions.prompt: Which level of Jannah is mentioned in the Quran and hadith as the highest?
questions.explanation: Firdaus is the highest level of Paradise; asking for it is encouraged.

questions.prompt: How many gates does Paradise have according to hadith?
questions.explanation: Paradise has eight gates; Hell has seven gates.

questions.prompt: Which prayer is the 'middle prayer' (Salat al-Wusta) mentioned in the Quran?
questions.explanation: Most scholars identify the middle prayer as Asr (2:238).

questions.prompt: What is 'Salat-ul-Eidain'?
options: The two Eid prayers with extra Takbirat
questions.explanation: The two Eid prayers include additional Takbirat and a sermon.

questions.prompt: Zakat is obligatory on which type of wealth?
options: Savings above Nisab held for a lunar year
questions.explanation: Zakat applies to qualifying wealth held above Nisab for one lunar year.

questions.prompt: What is 'Ushr'?
options: The 10% due on rain-fed agricultural produce
questions.explanation: Ushr is one-tenth on land watered by rain; half (5%) on irrigated land.

questions.prompt: What is the 'Hajj-e-Ifrad'?
options: Combining Hajj and Umrah with one Ihram
questions.explanation: Ifrad is Hajj alone; Qiran combines them in one Ihram; Tamattu' separates them.

questions.prompt: The black stone (Hajar-e-Aswad) is located in?
options: The eastern corner of the Kaaba
questions.explanation: The Hajar-e-Aswad sits in the eastern corner of the Kaaba.

questions.prompt: What is 'Multazam'?
options: The area between the Black Stone and the Kaaba door where dua is made
questions.explanation: Multazam is the space between the Hajar-e-Aswad and the door, a place of supplication.

questions.prompt: The 'Zamzam' well is located?
options: Inside the Masjid al-Haram, east of the Kaaba
questions.explanation: The Zamzam well lies within the Haram complex, about 20 m east of the Kaaba.

questions.prompt: Which prayer is prayed in congregation at Mina during Hajj?
questions.explanation: Pilgrims at Mina pray the five prayers shortened, without combining.

questions.prompt: The Asr prayer consists of:
questions.explanation: Asr has 4 Fard rakat.

questions.prompt: The Maghrib prayer consists of:
questions.explanation: Maghrib has 3 Fard rakat.

questions.prompt: The Isha prayer has how many Fard rakat?
questions.explanation: Isha has 4 Fard rakat plus 3 Witr.

questions.prompt: The Jumu'ah prayer has how many Fard rakat?
questions.explanation: Jumu'ah consists of 2 Fard rakat after the khutbah.

questions.prompt: The Witr prayer is how many rakat?
questions.explanation: Hanafi fiqh observes Witr as 3 rakat.

questions.prompt: The Taraweeh prayer has how many rakat in a night of Ramadan?
questions.explanation: Taraweeh ranges from 8 to 20 rakat by practice.

questions.prompt: The 'Adhan' is the:
questions.explanation: Adhan summons Muslims to prayer.

questions.prompt: The 'Tasbih' commonly recited after prayer is:
options: SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar (33 times each)
questions.explanation: The post-prayer Tasbih is 33+33+33.

questions.prompt: The 'Khutbah' of Jumu'ah is delivered:
options: Before the two rakat of prayer
questions.explanation: The Friday khutbah precedes the prayer.

questions.prompt: What is the ruling on missing Fajr prayer intentionally?
options: It is a major sin without valid excuse
questions.explanation: Leaving obligatory prayers is a major sin.

questions.prompt: Sajdah in prayer is performed:
questions.explanation: Each rakat has two prostrations.

questions.prompt: The 'Tashahhud' is recited:
questions.explanation: Tashahhud is recited in the sitting position.

questions.prompt: Zakat is given to how many categories of recipients?
questions.explanation: Surah At-Tawbah lists eight Zakat recipients.

questions.prompt: What is the ruling on giving Zakat to one's parents?
options: Not allowed (they are already your responsibility)
questions.explanation: Zakat cannot be given to dependants.

questions.prompt: The 'Fitr' charity before Eid-ul-Fitr is:
questions.explanation: Sadaqat-ul-Fitr purifies the fast.

questions.prompt: The stoning of the pillars at Mina is called:
questions.explanation: Rami symbolises rejecting evil.

questions.prompt: The circuit of the Kaaba during Hajj is called:
questions.explanation: Tawaf is circling the Kaaba seven times.

questions.prompt: The standing at Arafah is known as:
questions.explanation: Wuquf at Arafah is the core of Hajj.

questions.prompt: The Zuhr prayer has how many Fard rakat?
questions.explanation: Zuhr consists of four Fard rakat.

questions.prompt: The time of the Fajr prayer begins at?
questions.explanation: Fajr begins at the true (second) dawn.

questions.prompt: The time of the Isha prayer extends until approximately?
questions.explanation: Isha time lasts until about midnight in the common view.

questions.prompt: The Qunut supplication in Witr is recited?
options: In the last rakah before or after Ruku
At the beginning of the prayer
questions.explanation: The Qunut of Witr is recited in the final rakah.

questions.prompt: According to the Hanafi school, is Zakat due on gold jewellery?
questions.explanation: The Hanafi school holds that gold jewellery above Nisab attracts Zakat.

questions.prompt: Zakat on trade goods is calculated on?
questions.explanation: Zakat on merchandise is based on its market value at the end of the year.

questions.prompt: After Arafat, pilgrims spend the night of the 9th at?
questions.explanation: Pilgrims pray Maghrib and Isha combined and sleep at Muzdalifah.

questions.prompt: The tent city where pilgrims stay during the days of Tashriq is?
questions.explanation: Pilgrims spend the 11th-13th of Dhul-Hijjah in Mina.

questions.prompt: On the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah, pilgrims stone which pillar?
questions.explanation: Only Jamarat al-Aqabah is stoned on the Day of Sacrifice.

questions.prompt: How many pebbles are thrown at Jamarat al-Aqabah on the 10th?
questions.explanation: Seven pebbles are thrown at the big Jamrah on the 10th.

questions.prompt: The essential Tawaf of Hajj performed on the 10th is called?
questions.explanation: Tawaf al-Ifadah (Ziyarah) is a pillar of Hajj.

questions.prompt: The farewell circumambulation before leaving Makkah is called?
questions.explanation: Tawaf al-Wida is the farewell Tawaf for those leaving Makkah.

questions.prompt: The arrival circumambulation for a pilgrim is called?
questions.explanation: Tawaf al-Qudum is performed upon arriving in Makkah.

questions.prompt: The first rite of Umrah is?
questions.explanation: Umrah begins with entering the state of Ihram at the Miqat.

questions.prompt: What is the 'Miqat' in Hajj and Umrah?
options: The boundary where pilgrims enter Ihram
questions.explanation: Miqat is the appointed station where Ihram is assumed.

questions.prompt: Pilgrims arriving from the direction of Pakistan enter Ihram at which Miqat?
questions.explanation: Qarn al-Manazil serves pilgrims coming from the east, including Pakistan.

questions.prompt: Kissing or touching the Black Stone during Tawaf is called?
questions.explanation: Istilam is the salutation of the Black Stone.

questions.prompt: The semi-circular wall beside the Kaaba is called?
questions.explanation: The Hateem lies within the original foundations of the Kaaba.

questions.prompt: The corner of the Kaaba facing Yemen is called?
questions.explanation: The Rukn Yamani is the corner towards Yemen.

questions.prompt: Taking a bath (Ghusl) on Friday before Jumu'ah is?
questions.explanation: The Friday Ghusl is a strongly recommended Sunnah.

questions.prompt: Fasting six days of Shawwal together with Ramadan is like fasting?
questions.explanation: A good deed is multiplied tenfold, making Ramadan plus six days equal a year.

questions.prompt: Fasting on Mondays and Thursdays is?
options: Sunnah, as deeds are raised on these days
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) used to fast Mondays and Thursdays.

questions.prompt: How many Fard acts are there in Wudu according to the Hanafi school?
questions.explanation: The Hanafi Fard acts of wudu are washing the face, arms, wiping the head and washing the feet.

questions.prompt: On the days of Tashriq (11-13 Dhul-Hijjah), pilgrims stone?
questions.explanation: On the three days of Tashriq all three pillars are stoned.

questions.prompt: How many Jamarat (pillars) are stoned during Hajj?
questions.explanation: The three Jamarat are the small, middle and the big (Aqabah).

questions.prompt: The order of rites on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah is?
questions.explanation: The Sunnah order is stoning, then sacrifice, then shaving, then Tawaf.

questions.prompt: Wiping over the socks (Masah) is valid for how long for a resident?
questions.explanation: A resident may wipe over khuffayn for 24 hours; a traveller for three days.

questions.prompt: The 20-rakah Taraweeh in congregation was revived by whom?
questions.explanation: Umar (RA) revived the congregational Taraweeh of twenty rakat.

questions.prompt: The Aurah of a man in prayer is?
options: From the navel to the knee
questions.explanation: A man's Aurah is from the navel to the knee.

questions.prompt: The Aurah of a woman in prayer is?
options: The whole body except the face and hands
From the navel to the knee
questions.explanation: In prayer a woman covers everything except her face and hands.

questions.prompt: What is the reward of performing 'Umrah' during Ramadan according to a hadith?
options: It equals the reward of Hajj
questions.explanation: The Prophet (PBUH) said Umrah in Ramadan is equivalent to Hajj in reward.

questions.prompt: The 'Talbiah' is recited by pilgrims while entering and during?
questions.explanation: The Talbiah is the chant of Ihram, recited from the Miqat.

questions.prompt: How many days does the 'Hajj' essentially last?
questions.explanation: The Hajj rites span roughly the 8th to the 12th of Dhul-Hijjah.

questions.prompt: What is 'Salat-ul-Janazah'?
options: The funeral prayer with no ruku or sajdah
questions.explanation: The funeral prayer has four takbirs and no bowing or prostration.

questions.prompt: The 'Istisqa' prayer is offered for?
questions.explanation: Salat al-Istisqa seeks rain in times of drought.

questions.prompt: The 'Khusuf' prayer is offered during?
questions.explanation: Khusuf is the prayer of the lunar eclipse; Kusuf is the solar eclipse prayer.

questions.prompt: The 'Qasr' of prayers while travelling reduces which prayers?
questions.explanation: Zuhr, Asr and Isha are shortened to two rakat during travel.

questions.prompt: The 'Fidyah' for a permanently unable fast is?
options: Feeding one poor person per missed fast
questions.explanation: Those permanently unable to fast feed a poor person for each missed day.
